name: Dieppe raid, 1942
description: On Aug. 19, 1942, nearly 5,000 men of the 2nd Canadian Division raided this port. More than 900 were killed and nearly 2,000 captured. Clayton's division came back and freed the town on Sept. 1, 1944.

name: Juno Beach
description: One of the five D-Day beaches, where the 3rd Canadian Division landed on June 6, 1944. Clayton's regiment came ashore here, in the Mike sector at Graye-sur-Mer, on July 8.

name: Abbaye d'Ardenne
description: An old abbey west of Caen. In June 1944, soldiers of the 12th SS Division murdered about 20 captured Canadians here.

name: Verrières Ridge
description: The low ridge south of Ifs. Canadians attacked it in Operation Atlantic (July 19 to 21) and Operation Spring (July 25), at heavy cost. Clayton's K troop was destroyed here on July 20.

name: Bretteville-sur-Laize Cdn. War Cemetery
description: A Canadian war cemetery with nearly 3,000 graves. Most of the men of Clayton's regiment killed on July 20 and 21, 1944, are buried here.

name: Hill 262
description: The 1st Polish Armoured Division, fighting under First Canadian Army, held this hill from Aug. 19 to 21, 1944, blocking Germans trying to escape the Falaise pocket.

name: St. Lambert-sur-Dives (Currie's VC)
description: Maj. David Currie of the South Alberta Regiment held part of this village from Aug. 18 to 20, 1944, and won the Victoria Cross. Clayton told the Lacombe Globe he was part of Currie's force; the war diary can't confirm it.

name: Forêt de la Londe
description: A forest south of Rouen where Clayton's division fought German rearguards from Aug. 27 to 29, 1944, to clear the Seine crossings.

name: Boulogne
description: A Channel port the 3rd Canadian Division took by siege from Sept. 17 to 22, 1944, while Clayton's division was around Dunkirk.

name: Calais
description: A Channel port the 3rd Canadian Division took by siege from Sept. 25 to Oct. 1, 1944.

name: Walcheren
description: The island guarding the mouth of the Scheldt. Clayton's division fought onto its causeway from Oct. 31 to Nov. 2, 1944, before British troops took over.

name: Breskens
description: The south bank of the Scheldt. The 3rd Canadian Division cleared the Breskens Pocket in October 1944 in flooded, bitter fighting.

name: Nijmegen bridge
description: The bridge over the Waal, taken on Sept. 20, 1944, after American paratroopers crossed the river in canvas boats. Clayton spent the winter of 1944 nearby.

name: Groesbeek Canadian War Cemetery
description: A Canadian war cemetery with more than 2,300 graves, most from the battles of February and March 1945.

name: Goch
description: A German town flattened by bombing ahead of Operation Veritable and taken in late February 1945.

name: 20th Anti-Tank Battery Memorial
description: A memorial in Henderson Lake Park, Lethbridge, put up in 1996 by veterans of the 20th Battery, one of the four batteries of Clayton's regiment.

name: Pier 21
description: The Halifax pier where Clayton's troopships sailed in 1940, and where most war brides, likely including Lynda, landed in Canada. Today it's the Canadian Museum of Immigration at Pier 21.

name: Brookwood Military Cemetery
description: Near Aldershot, where the Canadian Army was based in England. It has the largest Canadian section of any war cemetery in Britain, mostly soldiers who died in training or accidents while they waited.

name: Juno Beach Centre
description: Canada's museum and memorial at Courseulles-sur-Mer, on the beach where the 3rd Canadian Division landed on D-Day. Opened in 2003.

name: Bény-sur-Mer Cdn. War Cemetery
description: About 2,000 Canadians who died on D-Day and in the first weeks in Normandy are buried here, near Juno Beach.

name: Bayeux Memorial
description: Names Commonwealth soldiers killed in Normandy who have no known grave, including Bdr. Callaghan and Gnr. Stewart of Clayton's regiment, killed July 21, 1944.

name: Dieppe Cdn. War Cemetery
description: At Hautot-sur-Mer, just south of Dieppe. About 950 men are buried here, most of them killed in the 1942 raid. Clayton's regiment held memorial services nearby in September 1944.

name: Calais Cdn. War Cemetery
description: At Leubringhen, between Boulogne and Calais. About 700 graves, most from the Canadian sieges of the Channel ports in September 1944.

name: Adegem Cdn. War Cemetery
description: In Belgium near the Dutch border. About 850 Canadians are buried here, many from the Breskens Pocket and Leopold Canal fighting in October 1944.

name: Schoonselhof Cemetery
description: In Antwerp. Its Commonwealth plot holds many soldiers from the Scheldt battles, including Sgt. Robert Earl Austin of Clayton's battery, died October 1944.

name: Bergen-op-Zoom Cdn. War Cemetery
description: About 1,100 Canadians are buried here, most killed in the Scheldt fighting north of Antwerp and on South Beveland in October 1944.

name: Holten Cdn. War Cemetery
description: About 1,400 Canadians who died in the last weeks of the war in the northern Netherlands and Germany, including the fighting toward Groningen and Oldenburg.

name: The Military Museums
description: Calgary's military museum, on the old Currie Barracks grounds near Sarcee Camp, where Gordon trained in 1940 and 1941.
